accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EEF guidance report Metacognition and Self-regulated Learning: recommendation 2 is to explicitly teach pupils metacognitive strategies, including how to plan, monitor and evaluate their learning, and the report names this metacognitive regulation. Every pace number in the lab is consistent: 20 in 30 minutes puts the plan line at 10 by the 15-minute check; Kai 5, Zoe 6 and Ava 11 at 15; Leo's 16 of 20 matches 4 red crosses.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips the EEF report and teachers flag at 9-10: checking only at the end (Mia), trusting a feeling of knowing over evidence (Kai feels fine at 5 of 20; Ana re-reads notes), persisting with a failing strategy (stuck on question 6), treating a change of course as giving up, vague goals (do some maths) and empty next steps (try harder, it went OK).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpme is the only lab built on a live pace graph: a dashed plan line from 0 to 20 over 30 minutes, an orange progress line per homework run, a draggable time line to the 15-minute check, a fix that visibly regrows the rest of the run, and a tappable lost-minutes band. lab_distinct gate passed against all other flagship labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner first sorts questions by when they are asked, then builds a checkable plan whose checkpoint (about 10 by 15 minutes) is the line used in the next step, judges three runs against it, repairs each with the change the graph calls for, and finally reads finished graphs to find lost minutes, so the cycle is built step by step before the done message names it.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions commit the learner before the reveal: when to ask is my strategy working (during, not only at the end), whether Kai at 5 of 20 who feels fine is on track (no, the plan says 10), and the best move when stuck for 9 minutes (skip and come back). Each is then tested directly on the graph.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with shuffled options; each wrong option has its own tagged hint (end, same, quit, vague, score, feel) that names the specific slip, such as feeling sure is not evidence, rather than a bare wrong, and the streak counter resets on a miss.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text passes the 6.5 Flesch-Kincaid target and the adult text was cut into shorter sentences to pass 9.5; validate_lessons reports no reading-level failure. Lab copy uses short words: plan, check, behind, on track, lost minutes, next time.

no_filler.evidence: No stock openers or journey language; each explain paragraph carries one step of the cycle with a concrete homework example (20 sums in 30 minutes, about 10 by halfway, phone in another room), and the content gate's filler and overlap checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13 and desktop with all 5 tasks completed via Show me; screenshots at 360 px wide (light) and on iPhone 13 (dark) show the graph axes, plan label, check line and done tags clear of each other, and plan or fix choices wrap in full-width buttons below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: axe returned no violations in light or dark theme on both viewports; every graph action has a button twin (Move to 15 minutes, On track, Mark minutes 6 to 16), the canvas aria-label and a live region speak each result, and colour is never the only cue because runs carry n done labels and crosses.
